questionText: Let WB and WT be two set associative cache organizations that use LRU algorithm for cache block replacement. WB is a write back cache and WT is a write through cache. Which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
options: Each cache block in WB and WT has a dirty bit.
Every write hit in WB leads to a data transfer from cache to main memory.
Eviction of a block from WT will not lead to data transfer from cache to main memory.
A read miss in WB will never lead to eviction of a dirty block from WB.
explanation:
Analysis of Options:

Statement (A): FALSE. Write-through (WT) cache updates main memory simultaneously with every write, so it does not need a dirty bit. A dirty bit is only required for write-back (WB) cache to track modified blocks.

Statement (B): FALSE. In a write-back cache, a write hit updates the block in cache and sets its dirty bit to 1; data is not immediately written back to main memory.

Statement (C): TRUE. In a write-through cache, main memory is always consistent with the cache. Therefore, evicting a block from WT never requires writing data back to main memory.

Statement (D): FALSE. A read miss in a write-back cache requires fetching a missing block into a set. If that set is full, an existing block must be evicted. If the evicted block is dirty, it will trigger a write-back to main memory. Thus, a read miss can lead to the eviction of a dirty block.

Since the question asks for the FALSE statements, the correct options are A, B, and D.
